# 2026 general election in Boone County, Indiana

*Generated by `scripts/analysis_2026.py` on 2026-11-13 from the published tables; every figure below is computed, none is typed.*

> **Provisional.** The 2026 figures come from the Clerk's election-night report (printed 11/3/2026 11:40 PM); provisional until the county certifies. They will be replaced by the certified canvass when it is posted, and this report regenerated.

## Turnout

| Boone County | 25,098 of 56,847 (44.2%) | 29,015 of 60,377 (48.1%) | +3.9 |
| Indiana House 24 | 1,887 of 3,819 (49.4%) | 1,857 of 3,730 (49.8%) | +0.4 |
| Indiana House 25 | 15,675 of 32,677 (48.0%) | 19,304 of 36,741 (52.5%) | +4.6 |
| Indiana House 28 | 1,062 of 2,567 (41.4%) | 1,049 of 2,541 (41.3%) | -0.1 |
| Indiana House 41 | 6,474 of 17,784 (36.4%) | 6,805 of 17,365 (39.2%) | +2.8 |

| Indiana Senate 29 | 10,603 of 20,596 (51.5%) | 12,323 of 21,234 (58.0%) | +6.6 |

## Statewide offices on both ballots, countywide

These offices were on every precinct's ballot in 2022 and 2026 and contested by both parties, so they are the like-for-like comparison. Margin = (Republican − Democratic) ÷ (Republican + Democratic). The candidates differ between years.

| Office | 2022 | 2026 | Shift (points) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Secretary of State | Republican +10.5 | Democratic +13.4 | 23.9 toward Democratic |
| Auditor of State / State Comptroller | Republican +27.6 | Republican +1.2 | 26.5 toward Democratic |
| Treasurer of State | Republican +25.6 | Republican +3.7 | 21.8 toward Democratic |
| U.S. House District 4 | Republican +25.6 | Democratic +2.1 | 27.7 toward Democratic |

| Year | Boone County margin |

| 2010 | Republican +49.9 |
| 2014 | Republican +45.7 |
| 2018 | Republican +33.1 |
| 2022 | Republican +10.5 |
| 2026 | Democratic +13.4 (provisional) |

## Precinct shifts, Secretary of State 2022 → 2026

Of 53 precincts, **53** shifted toward the Democratic candidate and **0** toward the Republican candidate; the median shift was 23.3 points toward Democratic. Map: `maps/swing_secretary_of_state_2022_2026.png`.

Largest shifts toward Democratic:

| Precinct | District | 2022 | 2026 | Shift (points) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Center 08 | House 41 | Republican +38.1 | Democratic +17.7 | 55.8 toward Democratic |
| Center 04 | House 41 | Republican +36.5 | Democratic +4.8 | 41.3 toward Democratic |
| Center 10 | House 41 | Republican +23.7 | Democratic +16.7 | 40.4 toward Democratic |
| Worth 2 | House 25 | Republican +14.9 | Democratic +25.0 | 39.9 toward Democratic |
| Center 11 | House 41 | Republican +30.4 | Democratic +7.2 | 37.6 toward Democratic |

No precinct shifted toward the Republican candidate. Smallest shifts:

| Precinct | District | 2022 | 2026 | Shift (points) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Eagle 08 | House 25 | Democratic +7.2 | Democratic +14.8 | 7.6 toward Democratic |
| Marion 2 | House 24 | Republican +40.4 | Republican +32.4 | 8.1 toward Democratic |
| Eagle 03 | House 25 | Democratic +32.6 | Democratic +43.6 | 11.0 toward Democratic |
| Union 2 | House 24 | Republican +20.4 | Republican +7.9 | 12.5 toward Democratic |
| Sugar Creek 1 | House 41 | Republican +31.5 | Republican +18.5 | 13.0 toward Democratic |

## Method and caveats

- Source: Boone County Clerk precinct reports, parsed and validated as described in METHODOLOGY.md. In the 2026 general, 1,246 of 1,246 single-winner precinct contests have candidate totals equal to the report's own printed contest total, and the precinct rows were also checked against the Clerk's separate countywide summary (`scripts/reconcile_all.py`).
- Only the two-party vote is in the margin; third-party and write-in votes are excluded (their share is in `analysis/2026_general_tables.csv`).
- Different candidates ran in each year, so a shift describes how the same places voted for different contests, not a change in any individual's support.
- District figures cover only the part of each district inside Boone County.
- Maps: `maps/margin_secretary_of_state.png`, `maps/margin_us_house_4.png`, `maps/statewide_offices_2022_2026.png`, `maps/turnout_2026_general.png`, and the interactive map.
